title: Cindervale city council votes on license-plate cameras

bench-and-bill.title: Cindervale city council approves license-plate cameras for a one-year trial
bench-and-bill.author: Owen Brightwater
body: Cindervale's city council voted 5-2 on Wednesday night to approve a one-year trial of license-plate cameras. The city will install 24 cameras at major intersections and on the main roads into town.

Under the ordinance, plate data must be deleted after 30 days unless it's tied to an open investigation. Officers will need a supervisor's sign-off to search the data, and every search will be logged.

The cameras will come from Corridor Vision, which will charge the city $86,000 for the first year. The police chief must report the results to the council by December 2027, when the trial ends unless the council renews it.
Council member Ruth Adeyemi-Clark, one of the two no votes, called the 30-day limit “far too generous for a trial.”
